title: Assessment of Electrical Brain Activity of Healthy Volunteers Exposed to 3.5 GHz of 5G Signals within Environmental Levels: A Controlled-Randomised Study
authors: Jamal Layla; Yahia-Cherif Lydia; Hugueville Laurent; Mazet Paul; Lévêque Philippe; Selmaoui Brahim
integrity_status: Exact held PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Acute far-field laboratory carrier and sham in selected healthy adults, measuring resting waking EEG rather than cognition, sleep diagnosis or chronic disease.
limitations: Selected healthy volunteers, a specified acute laboratory signal and physiological endpoints limit transfer to other populations, waveforms or clinical outcomes. Corrected-output reproducibility and full scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
citation: Jamal Layla; Yahia-Cherif Lydia; Hugueville Laurent; Mazet Paul; Lévêque Philippe; Selmaoui Brahim. Assessment of Electrical Brain Activity of Healthy Volunteers Exposed to 3.5 GHz of 5G Signals within Environmental Levels: A Controlled-Randomised Study 2023. DOI: 10.3390/ijerph20186793.

claims.text: Isolated nominal electrode differences did not survive the reported cluster-based correction in the resting EEG analysis. This distinction should remain visible alongside the overall nonsignificant pattern.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 and 14 to 16, statistical analysis, Discussion and Conclusions

claims.text: The tested laboratory exposure and resting physiological measurements do not establish effects on cognition, a clinical sleep disorder or chronic exposure. Complete scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.

title: Prenatal cell phone use and developmental milestone delays among infants.
authors: Divan HA, Kheifets L, Olsen J.
integrity_status: Exact held PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Historical Danish birth-cohort analysis of recalled maternal phone use during pregnancy and early maternally reported developmental milestones.
limitations: Late exposure recall, questionnaire-based outcomes, participation and missing data constrain interpretation. Numerical reporting differences remain unreconciled; same-cohort reports are not independent replications. Scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
citation: Divan HA, Kheifets L, Olsen J.. Prenatal cell phone use and developmental milestone delays among infants. 2011. DOI: 10.5271/sjweh.3157.

claims.text: The cohort report found no coherent overall adverse association or use-pattern gradient for the early reported motor and cognitive/language milestones. This observational pattern is not a universal prenatal safety finding.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 7 to 8, printed pages 346 to 347, Discussion and conclusion

claims.text: Infant milestone outcomes were recorded before the later questionnaire asking mothers to recall pregnancy phone use. Recalled behavior is not measured fetal absorbed dose, and the questionnaire outcomes are not a clinical developmental examination.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 4, printed pages 342 to 343, Methods

title: Do 50/60 Hz magnetic fields influence oxidative or DNA damage responses in human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells?
authors: Mustafa E, Makinistian L, Luukkonen J, Juutilainen J, Naarala J.
integrity_status: Exact held PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Power-frequency magnetic-field and sham comparisons in a human neuroblastoma cell line, with and without a menadione challenge; laboratory assays rather than recruited people or clinical disease.
limitations: Few independent culture experiments, exploratory unadjusted gene comparisons and unavailable supplementary tables limit interpretation. A lower fluorescence response after chemical challenge is not proof of cancer protection or human benefit. Scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
citation: Mustafa E, Makinistian L, Luukkonen J, Juutilainen J, Naarala J.. Do 50/60 Hz magnetic fields influence oxidative or DNA damage responses in human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells? 2022. DOI: 10.1080/09553002.2022.2055803.

claims.text: The report found no significant magnetic-field difference in comet-assay DNA damage or repair, or cytosolic superoxide. A lower chemically challenged ROS signal and small exploratory gene changes were observed without establishing a protective mechanism.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 10, Results, Figures and Conclusion

claims.text: The gene-expression screening was explicitly exploratory and used no multiple-testing correction. Results in transformed cell cultures do not establish human disease effects, and different significance results at the tested frequencies do not by themselves establish a frequency difference.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical page 5, Statistics; pages 8 to 10, Discussion and Conclusion
